dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — Calling because you'll be late
dialogs.intro: Budi is stuck in the rain and calls Bounmy. Notice that a Lao phone call opens with a completely different word from the everyday greeting.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ຮາໂລ|Haa-lóo] [ແມ່ນ|Mèen][ໃຜ|phǎi][ນໍ|náw]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຮາໂລ|Haa-lóo] [ບູດີ|Buu-dii][ເອງ|éeng] [ຟັງ|Fáng][ຄັກ|khak][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Hello, it's Budi. Can you hear me clearly?

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ຟັງ|Fáng][ບໍ່|bàw][ຄັກ|khak] [ສັນຍານ|Sǎn-nyáan][ບໍ່|bàw][ດີ|dii] [ເວົ້າ|Vâo][ດັງໆ|dang-dang][ແດ່|dèe]
lines.id: Not very clearly. The signal's bad. Speak up a bit.
lines.literal: hear — not — clear. signal — not — good. speak — loud-loud — a-little.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ດຽວນີ້|Dǐao-nîi][ຄັກ|khak][ບໍ່|bàw] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ຊິ|si][ມາ|maa][ຊ້າ|sâa][ໜ້ອຍ|nàwy][ໜຶ່ງ|nʉ̀ng] [ຝົນ|Fǒn][ຕົກ|tók][ໜັກ|nak]
lines.id: Is it clear now? I'm going to be a little late. It's pouring.
lines.literal: now — clear — (question)? I — will — come — late — little — one. rain — fall — heavy.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ຄັກ|Khak][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ບໍ່ເປັນຫຍັງ|Bàw pen nyǎng] [ຊິ|Si][ຮອດ|hâwt][ຈັກ|ják][ໂມງ|móong]
lines.id: Clear now. No problem. About what time will you get here?
lines.literal: clear — already. not — be — what. will — arrive — what — o'clock?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ປະມານ|Pa-máan][ເຈັດ|jét][ໂມງ|móong] [ຖ້າ|Thàa][ຝົນ|fǒn][ເຊົາ|sao] [ອາດ|àat][ຊິ|si][ໄວ|vái][ກວ່າ|kwàa][ນັ້ນ|nân]
lines.id: Around seven. If the rain lets up, maybe earlier than that.
lines.literal: about — seven — o'clock. if — rain — stop — maybe — will — fast — more — that.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ຊິ|si][ຖ້າ|thàa][ຢູ່|yùu][ຮ້ານ|hâan] [ຝາກ|Fàak][ບອກ|bàwk][ໝູ່|mùu][ໃຫ້|hài][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Okay, I'll wait at the restaurant. Should I tell the others?
lines.literal: can. I — will — wait — at — shop. entrust — tell — friend — give — (question)?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຝາກ|Fàak][ບອກ|bàwk][ແດ່|dèe] [ບອກ|Bàwk][ວ່າ|vàa][ຢ່າ|yàa][ຖ້າ|thàa][ຂ້ອຍ|khàwy] [ສັ່ງ|Sáng][ອາຫານ|aa-hǎan][ກ່ອນ|kàwn][ເລີຍ|lóei]
lines.id: Please do. Tell them not to wait for me — go ahead and order.
lines.literal: entrust — tell — a-little. tell — that — don't — wait — me. order — food — first — right-away.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi][ເລີຍ|lóei] [ສົ່ງ|Sóng][ຕຳແໜ່ງ|tam-nèng][ໃຫ້|hài][ຂ້ອຍ|khàwy][ໃນ|nai][ວອດແອັບ|wàwt-èp][ເດີ້|dòe]
lines.id: Sure. Send me your location on WhatsApp, okay?
lines.literal: can — right-away. send — location — give — me — in — WhatsApp — (friendly particle).

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi] [ເບີ|Bòe][ໂທ|thóo][ເຈົ້າ|jâo][ຄື|khʉʉ][ເກົ່າ|kào][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Okay. Is your number still the old one?
lines.literal: can. number — phone — you — like — old — (question)?

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ຄື|Khʉʉ][ເກົ່າ|kào] [ພົບ|Phop][ກັນ|kan][ຕອນ|tawn][ແລງ|léeng][ເດີ້|dòe] [ຂັບ|Khap][ລົດ|lot][ລະວັງ|la-wáng][ເດີ້|dòe]
lines.id: Still the same. See you this evening. Drive carefully.
lines.literal: like — old. meet — together — time — evening — (friendly particle). drive — vehicle — careful — (friendly particle).

notes: **ຮາໂລ haa-lóo is used ONLY on the phone.** Greeting someone in front of you with *ຮາໂລ* sounds odd. Face to face, stick with *ສະບາຍດີ*. The habit comes from French *allô*, and it's used across former Indochina.

**ຄັກ khak = "clear, good, neat", and it's a very Lao word.** *ຟັງບໍ່ຄັກ* (can't hear clearly), *ເບິ່ງບໍ່ຄັກ* (can't see clearly), *ຄັກແລ້ວ* (good, okay). In everyday speech, *ຄັກ* also means "cool": *ຄັກຫຼາຍ* (so cool).
**ເອງ éeng after a name = "it's me".** *ບູດີເອງ* is the most natural way to identify yourself on the phone — not *ຂ້ອຍແມ່ນບູດີ*, which sounds like reading out a document.

**ຝາກບອກ fàak bàwk = "leave a message, pass on word".** The word *ຝາກ fàak* means "entrust, leave with someone": *ຝາກເງິນ* (deposit money), *ຂອງຝາກ* (souvenirs — literally "entrusted things"). To ask someone to pass on a message: *ຝາກບອກລາວແດ່* (please tell him for me).
**ປະມານ pa-máan = "about, around".** *ປະມານເຈັດໂມງ* (around seven), *ປະມານສາມກິໂລ* (about three kilometers). It keeps your commitments loose in an honest way — and it's used all the time.
**ສັ່ງ sáng = "order (food, goods), tell (someone to do)".** *ສັ່ງອາຫານ* (order food), *ສັ່ງເຄື່ອງ* (order goods), *ສັ່ງໃຫ້ໄປ* (tell someone to go). Compare *ຈອງ jawng* (book, reserve) from unit 7.
**ດັງໆ dang-dang = "loudly".** Doubling an adjective in Lao both softens and clarifies it: *ຊ້າໆ* (slowly), *ໄວໆ* (quickly), *ດີໆ* (nicely, properly). It works a bit like English "nice and slow".

**ຄືເກົ່າ khʉʉ kào = "same as before, as usual".** A handy answer to any question about something that hasn't changed: phone number, address, how you're doing. *ສະບາຍດີບໍ່ — ຄືເກົ່າ* (how are you? — same old).

**About phones in Laos.** Two apps rule everything: **WhatsApp** for personal and work chats, and **Facebook** — *ເຟສບຸກ Fêet-búk* — for almost everything else, including shops, restaurants, and official announcements. Many small businesses in Laos have no website at all, only a Facebook page. Swapping Facebook accounts is as normal as swapping numbers.

after: Ending a call in Lao doesn't use a formal "goodbye". What sounds natural: *ໄປກ່ອນເດີ້* (I'm off, okay) or just *ໂອເຄ ເດີ້ ôo-khée dòe*.

sections.title: Writing short messages that sound natural

head: Lao
Say it
Meaning
When
rows: ສະບາຍດີເດີ້
ຮອດແລ້ວບໍ່
ຂໍໂທດມາຊ້າ

blocks.text: Lao texting is much shorter than spoken Lao. Pronouns are often dropped completely: *ຮອດແລ້ວບໍ່* without "you", *ກຳລັງໄປ* without "I". Writing full sentences in a chat actually sounds formal — much like in English.

Emoji are used a lot, and laughter is written in numbers: **555** — because the number five in Lao and Thai is *hāa*, so "555" is "ha ha ha". If someone sends you *555*, they're laughing, not sending a code.

blocks.text: Lao phone numbers are read **digit by digit**, not grouped into larger numbers. The number 020 5555 1234 is read *sǔun-sǎwng-sǔun hāa-hāa-hāa-hāa nʉ̀ng-sǎwng-sǎam-sìi*. All cell phone numbers start with **020**.
**ຕິດຕໍ່ *tít-taw*** means "contact" and *ຕິດຕໍ່ກັນ* means "stay in contact". *ຕິດຕໍ່ກັນເດີ້* is a warm, common way to say goodbye — like "don't be a stranger" in English.
